name: Hasan Piker
role: American left-wing Twitch streamer and political commentator (born 1991)
summary: Piker is a self-described Marxist and socialist commentator who supports public ownership, universal healthcare, workplace democracy and labor power, and opposes US imperialism and Zionism. He is critical of the Democratic Party establishment while backing left candidates such as Zohran Mamdani and engaging in electoral politics. He praises aspects of China's development and treats provocation as part of his streaming style.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Wikipedia records his support for universal health care and he campaigns for Medicare for All; also said healthcare should not run on profit.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Disagreed that preserving jobs should take priority over minimum wage increases, implying support for raising it; not a direct statement on the size of a rise.

public-ownership.rationale: Strongly agreed strategically important companies should remain under state control; per Wikipedia he advocates municipally owned infrastructure ("sewer socialism") on the TVA model.

unions-good.rationale: Urged labor mobilization and stressed that work stoppages are the working class's main power.

worker-ownership.rationale: Strongly agreed with the quiz item that large companies should belong to their workers rather than private owners.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Neutral/it depends on the stricter item that all drugs including cocaine should be legalized; no statement on recreational drugs generally.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Agreed that free speech should protect even offensive opinions; also agreed that accounts spreading false information could be removed.

strong-leader.rationale: Said he dislikes "the single leader thing" and rejected the single-leader-or-party option on how power should be organized.

limit-guns.rationale: Wikipedia lists support for gun control; degree not specified.

decide-locally.rationale: Neutral on local matters being decided locally and strongly disagreed that his country should be a union of regions with broad autonomy ("strong centralized command").

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Strongly agreed that LGBT couples should be able to show affection in public; Wikipedia records his support for LGBTQ+ rights.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Supports race-based quotas and diversity in public services, citing the value of lived experience.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Disagreed that he prefers preserving national traditions to accommodating foreign customs ("Who cares?").

free-trade.rationale: Disagreed that his country should pursue free trade agreements; the quiz item is about agreements, not the long-run claim.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Strongly agreed the government should limit imports that threaten local industry and jobs and agreed with limiting imports even if prices rise.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Said yes to the quiz item that the government should select and support leading domestic companies.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Called abolishing the central bank "insane" and strongly disagreed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Declined the single leader or party option, though joked that one- or two-party systems are fine "as long as the people are happy".

right-to-secede.rationale: On the stream quiz item "Regions should have a right to secede if local majorities vote for it" he answered neutral/it depends; later said the same about a no-secession item.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said "no" to political violence being acceptable but with a caveat that armed resistance by occupied populations may be treated differently.

separate-church-state.rationale: Strongly agreed that laws should be neutral and not follow the values of any religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Rejected emphatically that laws should reflect the values of the majority religion; item is about religious values, not scripture specifically.

military-superiority.rationale: Said US empire invests capital in weapons "far beyond any rational need" and welcomed its end.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Calls himself a Marxist, but no statement of his on whether class conflict drives history was found; a label isn't evidence.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Strongly agreed society should prioritize technological innovation and industrialization and rejected "back to nature".

accelerate-technology.rationale: Strongly agreed society should prioritize technological innovation and industrialization; chose balanced progress and nature in another item.

human-enhancement.rationale: Agreed that brain implants to enhance healthy people should be allowed and called himself "a little bit of a transhumanist"; defended gene editing to eradicate disease.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Rejected the back-to-nature, no-industry option, choosing a balance of progress and nature.

production-for-use.rationale: Strongly agreed that healthcare, education and water should not operate under the logic of profit; the statement is broader.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Described to the New York Times as Marxist/anti-capitalist; speaks of bosses and landlords extracting from workers; no single explicit sentence on profit as exploitation found.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Said at the Yale Political Union: "If a dictatorship is inevitable, I'd rather have it be a dictatorship of the proletariat" (conditional, as reported by Wikipedia).

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Links US imperialism and war spending to capital forces; stops short of the inevitability claim.

taxation-theft.rationale: Reacted with disbelief ("What kind of nonsense is this?") to the item that taxes should be voluntary.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Strongly disagreed that foreign policy should prioritize influence over neighbors and with threatening devastating military responses; describes US empire as something to end.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Calls himself a committed anti-Zionist and said Israel should not be an ally in its current form.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Wikipedia lists workplace democracy among his stated policy positions.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Disagreed with preserving national traditions over foreign customs; wants immigrants not judged by origin customs; quiz result showed strong multiculturalism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Described Israel as a "fascist settler colonial apartheid state" (as quoted by Wikipedia); stated about Israel, applied here to the general claim.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Strongly agreed that those who govern should have the consent and approval of the people affected.

separated-powers.rationale: Chose "democracy with checks and balances" as how power should be organized (while calling the options bad) and agreed independent judges should be able to overturn government decisions.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Praises strikes and work stoppages as workers' leverage; no statement on secret-ballot rules.

minority-language-support.rationale: Strongly agreed that different languages and cultures should coexist and that immigrants' children should be able to study in their parents' language in bilingual schools.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Answered "it depends" to preferring authoritarian rule if it accelerates development, citing India versus China.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Strongly disagreed that his country should develop nuclear weapons while saying it depends on the country; Axios: he does not want any nation to hold nuclear arms.

space-expansion.rationale: Agreed that space exploration should take lower priority than protecting the environment on Earth.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Attributes rising radicalism to "deteriorating material conditions".

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Strongly agreed with race-based quotas in university admissions and said he is "Mr. DEI" in opposing a ban on quotas for public jobs.

corporate-influence.rationale: Says the left cannot rely on corporations and blames corporate elites' profit-maximizing; no lobbying-specific statement.

non-intervention.rationale: After wavering (citing Israel and an international body), agreed that no country has the right to change another country's government.

suppress-opposition.rationale: On the stream quiz item "Governing efficiently matters more than guaranteeing space for the opposition" (about 4:05) he reacted "Ooh" and picked strongly agree on screen without reading it aloud; he then said efficiency and following the majority's wishes are "not at odds" and that one- or two-party systems are fine "as long as the people are happy". That item is milder than shutting down opposition and independent groups, and he elsewhere picked democracy with checks and balances and said he dislikes the single-leader option. He never said opposition or independent groups should be suppressed, so the evidence points both ways.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Supports workplace democracy and urges organizing and joining organizations.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Defends trans people against scapegoating ("Your landlord is not a trans person") and is recorded as supporting LGBTQ+ rights; no specific legal-recognition statement found.

alienated-labor.rationale: Describes young workers in jobs they despise with "no control"; implied critique of work under capitalism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Answered neutral/it depends to "My country should abolish its armed forces".

local-essentials-public.rationale: Strongly agreed that healthcare, education and water should not run on profit and rejected private provision of public services; supports municipally owned utilities ("sewer socialism").

capital-controls.rationale: Neutral/it depends on whether people should send money abroad without government permission (weighed tax evasion); item is the inverse of the statement.

close-ties-china.rationale: Visited China in 2025 saying the US could "adopt and emulate" from it; said a Chinese child may have better conditions than an American one.

notes: Quiz answers come from a 60-question quiz on stream (s1); he misread or joked on several items and those were excluded. Interview material (s3, s5, s6) is partly secondhand write-ups, so many positions stay null. Statements about Hamas, Oct 7 and China are contested and are not mapped to statements here without a direct match.
